correctness.rationale: For each integer b≥2, Lebesgue invariance is immediate from b equal full branches. Integration of the V-shaped f_b on each branch proves mean (2b−1)/(6b) and variance (2b²−2b−1)/(36b²). The transfer operator maps f_b to a symmetric continuous piecewise-affine function with corners at the fixed points j/(b−1); applying it again scales each derivative jump by b^−2. Symmetry and integral preservation force the remaining affine term to be constant, yielding the exact eigenidentity. A finite polynomial sum for ∫f_b P f_b establishes C_b(1)=(b−4)(b−2)(b²−b−1)/(180 b⁴). Duality gives C_b(n)=b^−2(n−1) C_b(1). Stationarity gives finite-N variance and its rational positive limit. A bounded u=∑Pⁿh exists explicitly; m=h+u−u∘T satisfies Pm=0. The reverse-martingale CLT plus bounded telescoping proves the Gaussian limit. Exact-rational independent branch integration tests 18 (b,lag) cases using verify.py; this is corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: Discrete finite-sum orbit path length is a natural arclength diagnostic. Existing recent literature motivates its convergence and rates, but effective calibration requires the precise asymptotic variance and serial-memory signs. The theorem supplies the full-lag covariance, finite-sample variance, exact zero-memory exceptions b=2,4, a strict negative b=3 regime and positive b≥5 regime, with a positive Gaussian scaling constant. This is a complete family-wide quantitative classification for an observable with direct motivation, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a claim that vanishing covariance means independence. It also exposes embedding dependence by explicitly choosing interval-coordinate displacement.
